source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Several fungal diseases affect watermelon:

Damping-off, which rots seedlings, is caused by Rhizoctonia solani, Pythium spp., and Cercospora spp.

Fusarium wilt, which rots the root system, is caused by Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. niveum, and shows as stem necrosis and gum/resin exudation on the stem (documented with reference photos labeled "Fusariose sur tige de melon: gouttes de gomme" and "Fusariose du melon: nécrose de la tige").

Alternaria leaf spot, causing leaf spotting, is caused by Alternaria cucumerina.

Gummy stem blight, affecting stems and vines (shown in a reference photo labeled "Chancre à Didymella"), is caused by Didymella bryoniae.

A cucumber/melon root and vascular wilt/decline disease is also referenced (illustrated with a photo labeled "Dépérissement du concombre"), consistent with soil-borne fungal root rot affecting cucurbits.

Control measures: soak seed in hot water at about 50°C for 15-20 minutes before planting; after 5-7 days of germination, apply fungicides such as Zineb, Mancozeb, or Captan at about 20g mixed in 15 liters of water, sprayed onto young watermelon seedlings. Avoid repeatedly planting the same cucurbit family crop on the same land. Seed can also be treated with fungicide such as Chloroneb mixed with the seed during storage; if disease appears after planting, fungicides such as Benomyl, Dinocap, or Thiophanate can be used.
